newsitem.title: GERMANY: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST - AUG 12.
newsitem.headline: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST - AUG 12.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

FRANKFURT - Deutsche Bahn AG, the German railways company, launches a new unit for advertising, design and marketing. Called Deutsche Bahn Medien GmbH, it will manage communication services and marketing and press work for Deutsche Bahn. (Horizont)

MUNICH - A study of brand-name products in Germany shows a direct relationship between the amount of money a company spends on ads and its success in the market. "The higher the media budget of a brand name is, the more successful it is," MediaGruppe Muenchen, a media marketing firm, says in the study. (Reuters)

MUNICH - The German computer and software industry doubled spending on advertising between 1993 and 1996 largely due to consumers' constant demand for information about new products, a market study finds. (Reuters)

FRANKFURT - The Bavarian State Authority for New Media declares some programming on German sports channel DSF inadmissible for including too much advertising for beer. The authority has asked the station to change the title of a programme called "Cheers to Schalke - The Veltins Bundesliga Magazine" (Evangelischer Pressedienst)
FRANKFURT - Ad agency J. Walter Thompson wins the media account of newly merged direct insurance companies Axa Direkt and Tellit Direkt. Tellit was previously represented by Optimedia. (Horizont)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:
MUNICH - Television group ProSieben Media AG declines comment on a newspaper report that it was in talks to take over the German subsidiary of Nickelodeon, the U.S. children's TV channel. (Reuters)

BERLIN - Berlin-based radio station RS2 says it hopes to repeat the success that U.S. and British radio stations have seen with a heavier regional focus by starting three separate broadcasts for a neighbouring state. (Reuters)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

BERLIN - Herlitz PBS AG, a stationary company, plans to start marketing a line of products emblazoned with the logos of 15 of Germany's soccer teams. A new unit of the company, Herlitz Merchandising GmbH, will distribute the products. The company hopes to reach turnover of 40 million marks ($21.5 million) with the new line. (Reuters)

SCHENEFELD - Retail group Spar Handels AG says it expects 1997 sales to rise about 10 percent after acquisitions boosted first-half revenue 13.1 percent to 6.88 billion marks. The company also says first-half operating profit before minorities rose 21.2 percent to 49.8 million marks, but expected demand in the grocery sector to remain soft for the rest of this year.
(Reuters)

DUESSELDORF - The head of Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (Dasa) is quoted as saying he wants to persuade France to help reshape the Airbus Industrie consortium into an integrated company to rival U.S. giant Boeing. (Reuters)
FRANKFURT - Shares in German tyre-maker Continental AG rise more than four percent after the company reported a 73 percent profit jump for the first six months of the year. (Reuters)
PEOPLE NEWS:
FRANKFURT - Ralph Ohnemus is named marketing director for Germany at Seagram's German unit in Hochheim. (Horizont)
FRANKFURT - Eckhard Schomber is the new advertising sales manager at Microsoft Network Germany. (Horizont)
Deborah Cole, Berlin Newsroom, 49-30-203-98114
